content: Gold is tested by fire, brave men by misfortune.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Vita Beata (On the Happy Life)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?
